title: Functional Evaluation of Genetic Variants Using Saturation Genome Editing
author: Obolenski, Olvera-León, et al.
materials: One Shot TOP10 chemically competent E. coli
NEBuilder HiFi DNA assembly master mix (2X)

steps.title: Design variant library and sgRNA
steps.instruction: Design an SGE variant oligonucleotide library covering each target region (≤245 bp) and a corresponding single‑guide RNA (sgRNA); include synonymous PAM/protospacer protection edits (PPEs) in each oligo to prevent re‑cleavage.

steps.title: Synthesize and amplify oligo pool
steps.instruction: Chemically synthesize the oligonucleotide pool, optionally amplify the whole pool with Primer Set 1, then amplify each target region using region‑specific Primer Set 2 to generate target‑specific SGE variant oligo libraries.

steps.title: Generate wild‑type homology vectors
steps.instruction: Amplify wild‑type homology regions of ~750–1000 bp flanking the 5′ and 3′ ends of each variant‑containing target region using Primer Sets 3 and 4.

steps.title: Create HDR template libraries
steps.instruction: Linearize the wild‑type homology vectors with Primer Set 5, then ligate the linearized vectors with the target‑specific SGE variant oligo libraries to produce the SGE HDR template libraries.

steps.title: Clone sgRNA into selection vector
steps.instruction: Clone each designed sgRNA into a vector that carries ampicillin resistance for E. coli selection and puromycin resistance for human‑cell selection.

steps.title: Transfect HAP1‑A5 cells
steps.instruction: In triplicate, transfect HAP1‑A5 cells with the appropriate HDR template library and the corresponding sgRNA‑containing vector.

steps.title: Select edited cells with puromycin
steps.instruction: Apply puromycin selection to the transfected cultures to enrich for cells that have incorporated the sgRNA vector and HDR template.

steps.title: Culture and sample time points
steps.instruction: Maintain the edited cell populations for 14–21 days, collecting genomic DNA samples at baseline day 4 and additional time points (days 7, 10, 14, 21) while keeping 5–6 million cells per replicate time‑point.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA from pellets
steps.instruction: Perform gDNA extraction from each cell‑pellet using the QIAGEN DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit with the following adapted steps:

substeps.instruction: Thaw cell pellets for each time‑point replicate.
Resuspend each pellet in 200 µL DPBS.
Add 4 µL RNase A (100 mg/mL) and incubate at 37 °C for 15 min.
Add 200 µL Buffer AL, vortex, then spin 300 × g for 30 s at 20‑25 °C.
Add 200 µL ethanol (96‑100 %), vortex, spin 300 × g for 30 s at 20‑25 °C.
Mix by pipetting up and down 5 times.
Transfer the entire 700 µL mixture to a DNeasy Mini spin column in a 2 mL collection tube; centrifuge at 9 500 RPM for 1 min.
Place the spin column in a new collection tube, add 500 µL Buffer AW1, centrifuge at 9 500 RPM for 1 min, discard flow‑through and tube.
Place the spin column in a new collection tube, add 500 µL Buffer AW2, centrifuge at 13 200 RPM for 1 min, discard flow‑through.
Centrifuge the same column again for 2 min at 13 200 RPM and discard the flow‑through.
Transfer the spin column to a clean 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Elute gDNA with 100 µL Buffer AE (use 50 µL Buffer AE if the pellet contained <5–6 million cells).
Centrifuge at 13 200 RPM for 1 min (viscous eluate).
Measure DNA concentration; expect ≥10 µg in 100 µL from a 5–6 million‑cell pellet.

steps.title: Prepare NGS libraries from gDNA
steps.instruction: Using the extracted gDNA, generate edited‑gDNA NGS libraries with Primer Sets 6‑8 as described in the key resources table, then proceed to sequencing and downstream analysis.
